speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To begin my assessment, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is your current neck pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (C5-C7). 

Based on your history of long-term neck pain, bilateral hand weakness, and paresthesias in the context of age and diabetes, this clinical picture strongly suggests cervical spondylosis compressing the spinal cord. To confirm this, please request a MRI of your cervical spine.
